sources.title: Better Infrastructure
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's Better Infrastructure programme covers physical and digital assets including transport, energy, water, waste, digital communications and flood-risk management across planning, funding, delivery and maintenance stages.

sources.title: Digital Connectivity Infrastructure Guidance
sources.verified_claim: The adopted guidance supports London Plan Policy SI6 by setting planning expectations for digital connectivity infrastructure in new and existing development, including integration and application information requirements.

sources.title: Digital and data programmes
sources.verified_claim: City Hall states Connected London works with boroughs and telecoms providers on gigabit connectivity and that new developments are required to have full-fibre connection, while wider data programmes support city services.

sources.title: Connected London
sources.verified_claim: Connected London focuses on full-fibre, mobile capacity including 5G, public Wi-Fi and future-proof digital infrastructure; its connectivity map highlights broad coverage challenges rather than parcel-specific service capacity.

sources.title: Local area energy planning in London
sources.verified_claim: Local Area Energy Planning coordinates electricity, heat, buildings, transport and network investment and is intended to inform borough Local Plans and utility investment so infrastructure can meet future needs.

sources.title: DD2727 Infrastructure Coordination Service – Integrated Water Management Strategies Programme
sources.verified_claim: The GLA approved support for Integrated Water Management Strategies to coordinate flood risk, water quality and water supply and inform planning policy; programme existence does not prove capacity at a sample parcel.

sources.title: Additional guidance on design and sustainability
sources.verified_claim: The housing funding guidance requires urban greening and heat-risk management for funded schemes and points to energy assessment and overheating modelling; this is programme guidance, not parcel consent.

sources.title: Air Quality Neutral guidance
sources.verified_claim: The adopted Air Quality Neutral guidance sets transport and building-emission benchmarks for development so proposals do not worsen London's air quality; compliance is proposal-specific.
